subject: sprinter
title: The 5 Fastest Humans Ever, Ranked (No One New Since 2015)

scenes.text: The five fastest humans ever timed. Nobody has broken into this list since 2015.

scenes.label: Justin Gatlin · 9.74 s
scenes.text: Number five: Justin Gatlin of the United States. 9.74 seconds in Doha in 2015, the newest time on the list.

scenes.label: Asafa Powell · 9.72 s
scenes.text: Number four: Asafa Powell of Jamaica. 9.72 seconds in Lausanne in 2008.

scenes.label: Yohan Blake · 9.69 s
scenes.text: Number three: Yohan Blake of Jamaica. 9.69 seconds in 2012, into a slight headwind.

scenes.label: Tyson Gay · 9.69 s
scenes.text: Number two: Tyson Gay of the United States. Also 9.69, three years earlier, in Shanghai.

scenes.label: Usain Bolt · 9.58 s
scenes.text: Number one: Usain Bolt of Jamaica. 9.58 seconds in Berlin in 2009. In a sport decided by hundredths, he leads by eleven.

description:
The five fastest humans ever, ranked by personal best over 100 metres with legal wind.
Usain Bolt (Jamaica) ran 9.58 seconds in Berlin on 16 August 2009. Tyson Gay (USA) ran 9.69 in Shanghai on 20 September 2009 and Yohan Blake (Jamaica) matched it in Lausanne on 23 August 2012, into a 0.1 m/s headwind. Asafa Powell (Jamaica) ran 9.72 in Lausanne in 2008 and Justin Gatlin (USA) 9.74 in Doha in 2015. Since then the closest anyone has come is Kishane Thompson of Jamaica with 9.75 in 2025; the fastest time of 2026 was 9.79.
Will anyone ever beat 9.58?
first_comment: Kishane Thompson missed this list by one hundredth of a second in 2025. Who do you think breaks in next, and what should we rank next?
